### 27.9 R09 production identity/session seam — pre-code boundary

Source decision: R09 is a verified repository gap, not a demand for a new auth vendor. WorkPlan lines 268–269 and 321 require external identity resolution and callback/session surfaces. The existing `OidcAuthAdapter` verifies credentials but `createSessionToken` is called by the development route only, which rejects OIDC mode. `SignInPage` intentionally delegates initiation to the deployment identity gateway; this provider-neutral ownership remains intact. ADR 0002 also says SameSite Strict while the existing development cookie is Lax; preserve that runtime contract and append an explicit ADR correction instead of claiming the historical wording matched implementation.

Owned repair/files: add `app/api/v2/auth/oidc/route.ts`, a same-origin POST credential-to-internal-session endpoint; reuse `createAuthenticateUser`, identity provisioning, signed session/key rotation and existing public rate limiting. Accept only one bounded compact JWT in an Authorization Bearer header (not URL, form, response body or storage); return only the existing fixed `/app` navigation target and an HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Lax cookie. Fail closed with content-free errors and no cookie on invalid credential, wrong origin/mode, rate limit, provider or database failure. This route cannot live in the development-only endpoint without weakening its explicit environment boundary.

Minimal supporting changes: require OIDC mandatory issuer/audience/subject/expiry/issued-at claims and authorized-party consistency in the existing `domains/accounts/infrastructure/oidc-auth-adapter.ts`; require HTTPS issuer/JWKS when deployed in `lib/env.ts`; append gateway integration and corrected cookie evidence to `docs/adr/0002-auth.md`. These are input/security checks at the existing adapter, not a new OAuth client. Gateway remains responsible for authorization-code/PKCE, browser-bound state/nonce, redirect registration, and obtaining an ID token for the configured Mythra audience; Mythra does not silently implement or assert production deployment of those external steps. Signing/verification rules are checked against [OpenID Connect Core ID Token validation](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#IDTokenValidation).

Positive proof: new tests must use real asymmetric signatures and a loopback JWKS server through `OidcAuthAdapter`, then the actual new route plus existing `AuthenticateUser` and identity repository to issue/read an internal cookie; repeated sign-in reuses identity/workspace with a fresh session. Negative proof: wrong issuer/audience/authorized-party, missing/expired claims, tampering, missing/oversized credential, wrong origin/mode, throttling and dependency failures yield no session and leak no token/claims/raw error; deployed insecure OIDC config rejects. Existing development auth, role/ownership, rotation, session, security and foundation tests remain unchanged. No schema, identity ownership, billing, UI workflow or domain authorization changes. Meaningful issuance/failure traces use adjacent S18 comments and the existing safe logger; exact lines will be indexed after verification.

R09 test-environment supplement: the initial five-suite run passed 17 tests and failed 17 OIDC signing fixtures before requests executed: JSDOM and Node TextEncoder produce different Uint8Array realms for JOSE. The production route is Node code. Run only the OIDC test in Vitest's native Node environment and guard the existing `tests/setup.ts` matchMedia stub with `typeof window !== "undefined"`. That single shared-test boundary change is necessary to run real cryptography without mocking verification; JSDOM component setup/cleanup and all existing assertions remain identical. The initial fixture failures are not counted as application regressions or successful security checks.

R09 native-proof supplement: `scripts/verify-s18-oidc-db.ts` will compose the real loopback JWKS verifier, existing AuthenticateUser and PrismaIdentityRepository against the isolated PostgreSQL 18 database. It must prove repeated verified credentials create one external identity/workspace, new session IDs, existing role re-resolution and cross-workspace rejection, plus no identity provisioning for tampered tokens. Only unique synthetic fixtures are written; the test closes its server/connections and logs counts/outcomes, not provider claims, tokens or database credentials. Add this verifier to the existing S18 isolated CI job; no deployment environment is touched.

### 27.15 R12c entity-arc Narrative Intent adapter — pre-code boundary

Bible V2.2 rendered page 11, section 3.7, explicitly permits optional Narrative Intent on an `entity arc`. The immediately preceding entity rule on the same rendered page establishes stable entities plus volume-specific state snapshots/scoped notes; it does not define a separate Entity Arc aggregate. WorkPlan S5/S9 requires the missing entity-arc target adapter. The implementation ruling is therefore exact and minimal: `ENTITY_ARC` is a Narrative Intent target type whose target identity is an existing active `StoryEntity` in the same project. It does not create an EntityArc table/domain, infer arc stages or progression, duplicate entities, mutate snapshots, or make Narrative Intent mandatory.

Expected production files: `prisma/schema.prisma` adds the enum member; a new forward/rollback migration adds and can remove it without touching other enum values; `domains/structure/domain/types.ts` exposes the validated target while retaining paragraph-only selection anchors; `domains/structure/application/ports.ts` adds a bounded, content-minimal eligible entity target summary; `domains/structure/infrastructure/prisma-structure-repository.ts` maps `ENTITY_ARC` to the existing active-entity endpoint check and includes eligible entities within the existing node budget; `components/structure/SemanticZoomViewport.tsx` presents those existing entities in the current Narrative Intent target controls and reuses the content-safe submission boundary. Generated Prisma client files may change only through `prisma generate` and are not hand-edited.

Expected proof files: `tests/service/structure-service.test.ts` proves schema acceptance and rejection of selection anchors on an entity arc; `tests/component/structure-interactions.test.tsx` proves an eligible entity can be selected and the exact `ENTITY_ARC` request is sent without logging intent text; `scripts/verify-structure-core-db.ts` creates only synthetic Universe records, proves native same-project active resolution and rejects archived/foreign entities, and extends its existing content-free database trace rather than adding a redundant operational boundary; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` invokes that existing Structure verifier after deploying every migration so the native proof is repeated remotely. Fixture-only `StructureOverview` files will add empty entity-target arrays as required by the stronger read contract.

Planned tests, in order: first add the service/component assertions and run them red against the missing enum/UI; implement the schema/repository/UI/migration; regenerate Prisma; rerun affected unit/service/component tests; deploy all migrations to native PostgreSQL 18 and run the extended Structure verifier; exercise the rollback SQL against an isolated disposable database or transaction-safe equivalent; then run lint, typecheck, full coverage and production build before claiming this defect closed. ### 27.17 R12c implementation, stress proof and local compliance decision

Observed test-first proof: before production edits, the focused service/component run passed 22 existing assertions and failed exactly the two new requirements. Implemented contract: `ENTITY_ARC` is now a durable `NarrativeIntentTargetType`. Its UUID resolves through the existing `ENTITY` endpoint adapter, which requires the `StoryEntity` to belong to the current project, have no archive timestamp and have `ACTIVE` status. The Structure overview exposes only bounded eligible `{ id, name, version }` summaries, charges them to the existing node budget, and orders them deterministically by name then UUID. The existing Narrative Intent form exposes `ENTITY ARC`, resets the target to the first eligible entity and submits through the unchanged service/API boundary. Paragraph selection anchors remain valid only for `PARAGRAPH_SELECTION`. No entity, snapshot, arc progression or authored text is inferred or duplicated.

Schema safety: migration `20260906135000_s18_entity_arc_intent` appends one PostgreSQL enum value. Its rollback deletes only rows that cannot exist under the prior enum, rebuilds the exact prior six-value enum and recreates `NarrativeIntent_selection_valid`. On a disposable clone of the synthetic database, rollback deleted one `ENTITY_ARC` row, restored `{PLOT,VOLUME,CHAPTER,SCENE,PARAGRAPH_SELECTION,MILESTONE}`, retained nine other Narrative Intent rows and retained the exact selection constraint. The disposable database `mythra_s18_r12c_rollback` was removed after verification and is intentionally not recoverable; the primary synthetic database was not rolled back.

### 27.20 R10 live operational alert evaluation and delivery — pre-code boundary

Exact verified defect: `lib/observability/alerts.ts` defines six thresholds, windows, severities, runbooks and hysteresis rules, but `evaluateAlert` has no production caller. `PrismaOperationsRepository.record` only inserts telemetry. Save telemetry records successful writes but emits no failure signal when repository save rejects. Backup and storage failures reach workspace operational events, while auth failure, global outbox lag and database saturation are emitted only as structured logs. `verify-release-readiness.ts`, unit tests and stress tests prove synthetic rule arithmetic, not live evaluation, durable state, transition delivery or delivery recovery. Therefore the prior S16/Phase-5 claim that operational alerts were implemented is weakened exactly as R10 states; existing content-safe instrumentation and rehearsal evidence remain valid and are not rewritten.

Owned repair: keep alerting inside the existing Operations/observability boundary. Extend the rule catalog with an explicit observation policy: fixed-window matching-event count for save/auth/storage failures, latest failure status for backup, and latest numeric gauge for outbox lag/database saturation. Add durable per-scope alert state and a transactional transition-delivery outbox. Workspace events evaluate in their workspace scope immediately after accepted telemetry; system-only auth/outbox/database signals evaluate in one explicit global scope. Evaluation uses the existing hysteresis function. State transitions enqueue one idempotent delivery version; the existing content-safe structured logger is the default provider-neutral delivery adapter. Immediate delivery is attempted, failed delivery remains retryable with bounded claim leases/backoff, and a small worker drains pending/expired deliveries. This is operational alert plumbing, not a user messaging system or external-vendor integration.

Expected core files: `lib/observability/alerts.ts` owns pure observation/window rules and the delivery adapter contract; `prisma/schema.prisma` plus one additive forward/rollback migration own only alert state/delivery records; `domains/operations/application/ports.ts`, `service.ts`, and `infrastructure/prisma-operations-repository.ts` own state evaluation, transition enqueue/claim/complete/fail, bounded admin reads and retry orchestration; `lib/operations/runtime.ts` exposes the existing repository-backed service and a global-signal boundary. `components/operations/AdminOperationsPanel.tsx` may display bounded current alert metadata on the already restricted admin surface. `scripts/process-operational-alerts.ts` performs only bounded retries. `package.json`, the incident runbook and S18 CI job may add the worker/verifier commands.

Necessary external producers are strictly limited: `domains/writing/application/durability.ts` emits a content-free `writing.save` failure event before rethrowing the unchanged error; both auth routes feed the existing `auth-failures` rule without credentials/claims; `app/api/v2/health/ready/route.ts` feeds the measured saturation gauge while preserving readiness status; `scripts/process-live-model-outbox.ts` feeds the already calculated lag gauge. R11 remote closure: commit `503564531715185a43c788c2a0515df0b218d571` was pushed and the local branch, `origin/agent/workplan-subgates-audit`, and PR head all resolved to that exact hash. This supersedes 27.19's pending qualifier: **R11 is REMOTE VERIFIED**.

R10 original claim and disproof: S16/Phase 5 previously called the alert catalog and synthetic release rehearsal “operational alerts.” Direct call-site analysis established that no production caller evaluated the catalog, no durable alert state or transition delivery existed, rejected saves emitted no failure event, and the global auth/outbox/database producers only logged. The implementation therefore proved instrumentation and rule arithmetic, not the WorkPlan line 662–663 requirement that observability detect the failures and that operational alerts be verified. Root cause was an incomplete seam between the typed OperationalEvent catalog and the pure `evaluateAlert` function, compounded by a stale Path claim that treated rehearsal as delivery evidence.

Implemented repair: every accepted alert-relevant workspace event is now stored and evaluated transactionally under a per-scope/per-rule PostgreSQL advisory lock. Save/auth/storage counts use bounded fixed windows; backup uses latest verified/failed status; outbox and database use latest bounded gauge. Existing threshold, recovery, severity and runbook values are unchanged. State changes create a unique `(alertStateId, transitionVersion)` delivery row; stable states do not. A provider-neutral structured-log adapter attempts delivery immediately. Failure persists only `ALERT_DELIVERY_FAILED`, uses a 30-second lease and exponential retry capped at five minutes. The bounded worker reclaims expired leases and expires count windows. Save/backup/storage are workspace-scoped; pre-session/system auth/outbox/database signals are explicitly global. The existing restricted admin surface reads at most 50 current workspace-or-global states and adds no manuscript/world data.

External producer behavior remains failure-isolated. A repository-rejected draft save emits one content-free failure event and rethrows the identical error; input-schema rejection occurs before incident timing/evaluation and is not misclassified as a storage failure. Development and OIDC auth failures feed the global count, but alert failure is caught and cannot change their existing safe HTTP response. Readiness feeds the measured database percentage, or zero when the metric is unavailable, without changing 200/503 selection. The projection worker feeds the already measured oldest-outbox age and catches alert failure so completed projections are not invalidated. Existing snapshot and research-storage service events reach the repository-backed workspace evaluator without producer changes.

### 27.24 R08 implementation, corrections, and post-code audit

R08 converts the pre-code boundary above into a complete, typed, locale-aware presentation contract. The English catalog is canonical and exhaustive. The Arabic catalog preserves every previously approved Arabic shell translation and fills every otherwise-untranslated key through an explicit typed English fallback; no fabricated Arabic product translation was introduced. The final merged catalogs contain exactly 1,145 English keys and 1,145 Arabic-resolvable keys.

The implementation migrated static user-facing copy across all inventoried product pages and components. Client surfaces consume `useMessages`; server pages consume the request-scoped catalog. Interpolation is centralized and typed. Locale-aware date, number, currency, percent, and byte formatters replace host-locale or hard-coded formatting at real-world presentation boundaries. Dynamic authored material, entity names, project names, manuscript text, research content, search input, Capture content, and other user data remain byte-for-byte presentation values and are never translated or logged.

Deep application/domain values that reach presentation are now locale-neutral codes or structured presentation metadata. Causality endpoint failures, context exclusions/directives, live-model warnings, search labels, milestone roles, structure scaffolding, universe built-ins/templates, portability issues, and writing-command failures resolve to resource-owned labels at the UI boundary. Custom author-defined universe labels and relation labels remain authoritative. The directive projection keeps first-class `becauseItems[]` and `consequenceItems[]`; neither is collapsed into ranked context. Semantic Zoom uses the locked coordinate order `Plot -> Plot Outline -> Volume -> Volume Outline -> Milestone/Thread -> Chapter Outline -> Chapter -> Scene -> Prose`, while milestones remain cross-cutting ownership objects.

Playwright's link auto-scroll immediately before click could overwrite the last stable author snapshot, so back-navigation restored the wrong position. | Verified product defect | Debounced scroll capture, freeze-on-navigation, timer cancellation, and navigation-safe cleanup were added. The exact continuation browser proof and the complete browser matrix pass. |

This did not break runtime behavior, but it made the native proof semantically false. | Verified evidence defect | The verifier now tests missing active endpoint IDs, requires every adapter to return `NOT_FOUND`, fails if any do not, and emits `missingActiveEndpointsRejected: true`. The complete PostgreSQL 18 native proof passes. |

The first complete browser run correctly exposed five issues: three localized expectation drifts, a scaffold punctuation defect, and the continuation defect above. The expectation drifts were updated to the resource-owned output (`Unmute Chapter outline`, locale-formatted `6,000 words · Sep 1, 2026`, and localized milestone roles); the semantic-zoom regression now selects `Milestone/Thread` before asserting milestone nodes. `BulkScaffold` no longer adds punctuation around a resource whose value already owns the colon. A first continuation repair was insufficient because browser auto-scroll precedes the click event; the final debounce/freeze design closes that timing window. No failed run was discarded or represented as a pass.

### 27.30 R17 controlled numeric-input regression — post-S18 discovery boundary

After S18 closure, live local use exposed a React development error at `components/structure/OutlineLens.tsx`: “Received NaN for the value attribute.” The supplied screenshot identifies the Order input. Source inspection confirms the cause: clearing a number input makes the browser's `valueAsNumber` return `NaN`; the component stores that non-finite value and passes it back to React as a controlled `value`. The same direct assignment pattern exists in `BulkScaffold`, `MilestoneLens`, and the paragraph-selection controls in `SemanticZoomViewport`, so repairing only the reported line would leave the identical defect reachable elsewhere.

R17 is a **Verified product defect** discovered after the prior finite register closed. This append-only entry does not erase the prior evidence; it supersedes the current S18/S19 state while the new defect is being repaired. **S18 is REOPENED; R17 IN PROGRESS; S19 RELOCKED; S20 LOCKED; PHASE 7 INCOMPLETE.**

## 28. Phase 7 Sub-gate 19 — Premium Visual Product Polish

### 28.1 S19 authority, invariant boundary, and slice order

S19 began only after the exact S18 closure proof in 27.35. Its authority is visual only: make the current Mythra product feel like quiet premium editorial software while preserving every current route, major surface, hierarchy, information architecture, workflow, capability, command/Search ranking rule, editor/durability/continuation behavior, persistence contract, schema, domain semantic, pricing decision, security/privacy boundary, and zero-AI deterministic Core rule. Writing remains sovereign, the manuscript remains the center of gravity, Structure remains optional power, and guidance/causality remain peripheral and optional.

Work will follow the bounded internal slices in the user-authored Phase 7 contract: A shared tokens/primitives; B shell/navigation/Project Home; C editor chrome; D Structure/Milestones/Causality; E Universe/Timeline; F Capture; G Search/Ctrl+K; H Context/Relevant Now/Peek; I Notes/Research; J billing/settings/operations/supporting surfaces; K responsive consistency; L cross-product consistency. These are review slices, not new capability gates. Each slice requires rendered before/after inspection, exact file ownership, positive and negative proof, affected interaction/accessibility checks, diff review, commit/push, remote evidence, and a Path.md entry before the next slice starts.

The Creative Production skill was inspected because this is a visual-polish task. Its mounted-board route is intended for generated image assets and no board tool is callable in this workspace; S19 needs repo-native HTML/CSS refinement and explicitly does not need generated bitmap assets. Its review discipline is therefore applied through real Mythra browser renders, not an image-generation board. The Browser/Computer Use transport became unavailable after the completed R17 live check, so the same installed Chromium used by Mythra's Playwright suite is the deterministic fallback for S19 captures; each artifact is then opened at original resolution for manual inspection.

### 28.9 S19-B remote regression discovery, correction, and revised local audit

The first S19-B implementation object was `3c7e280c4982406b1c9175eff5d57809b3a806a0`; local `HEAD` and `origin/agent/workplan-subgates-audit` matched that exact object before remote evidence was evaluated. S19-B therefore remained open and no remote-pass claim was made.

The uploaded `s18-browser-evidence` artifact was downloaded to ignored `tmp/s19-b-ci-timeout/` and inspected. Seven retained `error-context.md` files showed that mobile command-palette clicks were repeatedly intercepted by manuscript or `.mobile-writing-actions` descendants. The clearest traces reported the visible palette options `Quick Capture` and `Open Structure` waiting for actionability while a manuscript paragraph or the fixed `Capture` writing-action button received pointer events. Each affected test had a 150-second limit and CI allowed two retries; repeated interception consumed the enclosing job budget. A separate interrupted mobile Capture symptom and one desktop continuation symptom occurred inside the same resource-amplified run and were included rather than discarded.

The regression was traced to the S19-B-only `z-index: 10` added to `.command-bar`. `CommandPalette` is rendered inside that grid item. The grid item's explicit z-index created a parent stacking context, trapping `.command-palette-backdrop` (`z-index: 110`) below the root-level fixed `.mobile-writing-actions` (`z-index: 15`) despite the palette's larger local z-index. The correction removes only the `.command-bar` z-index declaration from `app/globals.css`; its 48px grid row, content, padding, border, background, shadow, control geometry, and all behavior remain unchanged. The palette now participates in the root stacking order and its existing `110` layer correctly covers the mobile writing bar. No component, DOM node, route, action, state machine, test threshold, retry rule, workflow timeout, or capability contract was changed to obtain the pass.

#### Failure and correction chronology

1. The first reduced-motion harness compared the serialized duration to the literal string `0.00001s`; Chromium serialized the same value as `1e-05s`. The corrected numeric assertion passed. No source changed for that harness error.
2. Initial computed geometry measured `.editor-layout` at 780px but the Tiptap wrapper and prose at 917px. The grid's implicit min-content behavior was the cause. The explicit `minmax(0, 1fr)` track plus the stable `editor-canvas` class corrected layout/canvas/prose to 780/780/780 without changing document behavior.
3. The first complete 74-case browser matrix passed 40, intentionally skipped 33, and failed the desktop Context test only after Peek return: the taller writing surface made the browser scroll the window from 141px to a lower card before `openPeek` captured 499px. An isolated rerun reproduced the same 141-to-499 mismatch. The wide Context reservation now owns that scroll, so the unchanged exact route/history/selection/scroll assertion passes.
4. The first isolated rerun after Context containment advanced past exact return, proving the original defect corrected, then found the new pin bar outside the clipped reservation after pinning. The card itself visibly changed to `Pinned`; the navigation was above the independent scroll position. Making only `.pin-bar` sticky preserved the existing preference state and made the unchanged navigation assertion pass. The final isolated test passed in 15.7 seconds and the full matrix passed.
5. A supplemental geometry harness searched for a nonexistent `[role="option"]` in the command list and terminated before its palette measurement. Source inspection confirmed the existing stable hook is `[data-palette-option]`; the corrected harness passed and confirmed the palette row is topmost. No product or test code changed for this harness error.
6. The first combined geometry report measured Focus immediately after the click and captured a transient outer-grid value. A focused rerun waited for `.editor-layout.focus-mode`; final bounds were outer fixed layer 1440px with 330px inline padding and a 780px grid track, while `.editor-canvas` and `.editor-prose` were each exactly 780px. This was an evidence-timing correction, not a source correction.

#### Negative evidence and corrections retained

1. The first visual-harness run failed because a fresh browser context was not authenticated. No visual conclusion was accepted. The ignored harness was corrected to use the real development sign-in flow before opening Structure.
2. The next run timed out at `networkidle` because the development server retained background requests. No visual conclusion was accepted. Readiness was corrected to `DOMContentLoaded` plus the actual `.structure-workspace` contract.
3. The first successful geometry run measured the mobile `Return to writing` control at 36px and a native checkbox at 13px. The product defect was corrected by making the mobile return action 44px. The audit correctly treats the associated checkbox label, not the browser-native checkbox rectangle, as its usable target; final non-native undersized-target results are empty.
4. An initial multi-theme Axe run reported inconsistent contrast after the harness directly mutated `data-theme` while the live Theme Provider retained different state. This was a harness defect, not accepted product evidence. Theme setup was corrected to use the actual theme selector, including a forced selection only where that existing selector is visually hidden on mobile, and to wait for the canonical document theme. The complete final matrix has zero serious/critical violations.

#### S19-E owned problem and baseline

S19-E owns visual refinement of the existing optional Universe workspace, entity detail/history surface and Timeline workspace. It may improve hierarchy, density, form grouping, authored-object presentation, chronological scanning, mode/status presentation, return actions, responsive flow and interaction states. It may not change entity templates or required minima, field optionality, entity/reference truth, relation direction, immutable snapshots, backlinks, Timeline modes, author-owned display labels, sortable coordinates, explicit links, chronology/causality separation, structural versions or any command/Context/editor contract.

The implementation follows the installed Next.js 16.3.4 guidance in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/11-css.md` and `node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/accessibility.md`: keep the existing root-imported global stylesheet predictable through component-scoped prefixes, verify production CSS ordering with `next build`, retain descriptive page headings and run JSX accessibility linting plus rendered accessibility checks.

#### Exact implementation contract

**Owned outcome.** Universe must read as optional world context rather than a narrow administration form: the identity/return context should be coherent, optional creation utilities should remain subordinate, authored entities should scan as a catalog, and entity truth/history should be distinguishable from authoring forms. Timeline must foreground chronology without implying causality: mode-specific creation, explicit non-causal linking and the ordered event record should have separate visual roles, while all five modes and author-owned labels remain unchanged. Both surfaces must use the available main region, remain calm beside the untouched 340px Context reservation, and retain every current field/action.

**Expected files.** `app/globals.css` is the expected visual owner. `components/universe/UniverseWorkspace.tsx`, `components/universe/EntityDetail.tsx` and `components/timeline/TimelineWorkspace.tsx` may receive stable presentation-only class hooks where positional selectors would be brittle. Tests change only if a genuine previously untested visual/accessibility contract is discovered. `Path.md` is required. No domain, service, repository, route, schema, migration, command, ranking, pricing, entitlement or infrastructure file is expected.

**Protected behavior and negative scope.** Preserve Universe zero-setup optionality; type-and-name minimum; system/project templates; optional fields; Unicode/RTL values; optimistic entity/structural versions; directional explicit relations; editor entity quick-create/reference behavior; immutable state snapshots; backlinks and stable identities. Preserve Absolute, Approximate, Relative, Ordinal and Range Timeline modes; author-owned display labels; sortable coordinates; deterministic order; relative anchors; explicit Timeline links; neutral chronology wording; no causal inference; bounded reads; Live Model events; Context endpoint projection; exact return to chapter/project; offline read-only behavior; Ctrl+K adapters; routes, request/response contracts, accessibility names/roles/order, telemetry payloads and privacy. S19-F and later surfaces, the Context reservation and shared tokens remain untouched.

**Required evidence before closure.** Enumerate every changed selector/hook and major consumer; render Universe list, entity detail and Timeline before/after across Light/Dark/Cream, desktop/mobile, empty/populated, long content, all five Timeline modes, custom-type disclosure, optional custom fields, immutable states, relations/backlinks, relative/range conditional controls, explicit-link form, status/error/disabled states where reachable, focus, reduced motion, 200% text and RTL. Measure no horizontal overflow and at least 44px mobile interactive targets. Run Universe, Timeline, editor reference/quick-create, Causal non-conflation, Context, Ctrl+K, continuation, responsive, accessibility, privacy/logging and stress regressions; complete coverage, lint, typecheck and production build; retain failures/corrections; inspect exact diff; commit/push; require exact-hash CI/Security and independently verified closure ledger before S19-F.

**Shared CSS safety.** Any rule in `app/globals.css` must remain prefixed by `.universe-workspace`, `.entity-detail` or `.chronicle-workspace` except an already-owned responsive grouping. Exact selectors, consumers and rendered non-interference will be recorded after implementation. Shared tokens, shell/editor/Structure/Capture/Search/Context/Research selectors and the 340px reservation may not change.

**Console/comment contract.** Presentation CSS is not a lifecycle boundary, so no new `console.log` is expected.
